title: Check data before trusting its type

outcomes.can: Predict runtime validation results and explain why an assertion cannot validate a field.

intro: An outside value can be anything. unknown lets you hold it while requiring evidence before reading fields. any turns off those checks. A type assertion written with as tells the compiler what to assume. Neither an assertion nor a type annotation examines the actual data. Validate the parts your program will use.

steps.title: Trace the example
steps.text: typeof null is "object", and arrays are objects too. The guard rejects null and arrays before inspecting properties. The in operator checks whether an object has a property. After checking typeof value.title, TypeScript knows the field is text. The JavaScript comparisons still execute after the type annotations disappear.

steps.title: Read only a valid title
steps.text: Return the title of a non-null, non-array object when title is a string, including empty text. For every other JSON value return null.

steps.title: Accept only complete imported tasks
steps.text: Use the contract in the exercise and check your answer on save.

choices.feedback: An empty string is still text and seven is a number.
The check examines the type, not the truthiness.

questions.prompt: Would an assertion as { title: string } change a numeric title to text?

choices.text: No. Runtime data stays the same.

review.evidence: Use a fresh answer on a later visit. An unaided pass on the changed case adds independent evidence. Preserve hint use and solution reveals with their attempts.
